subject: botany_2
question_text: Which one of the plant growth regulators would you use if you are asked to (a) induce rooting in a twig (b) quickly ripen a fruit (c) delay leaf senescence (d) induce growth in axillary buds (e) bolt a rosette plant (f) induce immediate stomatal closure in leaves (g) overcome apical dominance (h) kill dicotyledonous weeds?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.27, printed question 25. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Eight one-word answers, half a mark each. Answer every part even if you are unsure — a blank scores nothing, and a named hormone that is close often scores something.

steps.label: Parts a and b
steps.margin_note: Repeat the part letter with each answer so nothing is mismarked.
lines: AUXIN, such as IBA or NAA.
steps.why: A twig has no root tip to make its own auxin, and a fruit ripens on ethylene, so each answer names the hormone that does that one job.
common_mistakes: Answering (a) with gibberellin. ROOTING is an auxin effect.
Answering (b) with abscisic acid. RIPENING is ethylene.
steps.memory_tip: Rooting is auxin; ripening is ethylene.

steps.label: Parts c and d
steps.margin_note: Two parts, one hormone. Say cytokinin for both without hesitating.
steps.why: Both are cytokinin because both are about keeping tissue actively dividing rather than letting it age or stay suppressed.
common_mistakes: Answering (c) with ethylene. Ethylene PROMOTES senescence; cytokinin delays it.
Answering (d) with auxin. Auxin SUPPRESSES axillary buds.
steps.memory_tip: Cytokinin keeps things young and keeps side buds growing.

steps.label: Parts e and f
steps.margin_note: Two parts. ABA is also called the stress hormone, which is worth adding.
steps.why: Bolting is internode elongation, which is gibberellin's signature effect, and immediate stomatal closure is the one thing abscisic acid is named for.
common_mistakes: Answering (e) with auxin. Bolting is a GIBBERELLIN effect.
Answering (f) with cytokinin. Stomatal closure is ABSCISIC ACID.
steps.memory_tip: Bolting is gibberellin; shutting the pore is ABA.

steps.label: Parts g and h
steps.margin_note: Two parts. Naming 2,4-D specifically is better than writing 'auxin' alone.

lines.text: Auxin suppresses buds; cytokinin releases them

steps.why: Part (h) is the one trap in the list: the answer is an auxin, even though (d) and (g) were about escaping auxin's effect.
common_mistakes: Answering (h) with ethylene. 2,4-D is the weedkiller, and it is a synthetic AUXIN.
Answering (g) with auxin. Auxin CAUSES apical dominance; cytokinin overcomes it.
steps.memory_tip: The same family both suppresses buds and kills weeds: auxin does both.
